name: Luft
tagline: A desk air monitor you build in an evening
summary: Luft sits on your desk and shows temperature, humidity and air pressure on a small OLED. Press the button to cycle through readings and a 24 hour trend. It runs from any USB charger and keeps its data on the device.

connections.why: Power carries on to the sensor
Ground carries on to the sensor
The sensor shares the data line
The sensor shares the clock line
Pressing the button pulls the input to ground

firmware.behaviour: Read the BME280 every 10 seconds. Show temperature large, with humidity and pressure below. A button press cycles: now, 24 hour temperature trend, 24 hour pressure trend. Dim the display after 60 seconds without a press.

showcase.headline: Know your air. At a glance.
showcase.subhead: Temperature, humidity and pressure on a small display that sits on your desk. Four parts, one evening, no cloud account.

howItWorks.title: Plug it in
howItWorks.body: Any USB charger or laptop port powers it. It starts measuring within two seconds.

howItWorks.title: Glance at it
howItWorks.body: The current temperature is always on screen, with humidity and pressure underneath.

howItWorks.title: Press for history
howItWorks.body: One button cycles through the last 24 hours as a simple trend line.

features.title: Stays on your desk
features.body: Readings and history live on the device. Nothing is sent anywhere.

features.title: Four standard parts
features.body: A controller, a display, a sensor and a button, all sold by more than one shop.

features.title: A case that fits
features.body: The printed enclosure is generated from the same part dimensions as the guide.

features.title: Drawn to scale
features.body: Every step of the guide shows the real pads in their real positions.

features.title: Tested before it runs
features.body: A bring-up sketch reports each part it finds before the real firmware goes on.

features.title: Yours to change
features.body: One project file drives the wiring, the case and the firmware pin map.

stats.label: from bag of parts to working

faq.q: Do I need to have soldered before?
faq.a: No. The guide starts with how to make a good joint and what a bad one looks like, and every connection is drawn with a close-up of the exact pad.

faq.q: Can I build it without a 3D printer?
faq.a: Yes. It works on the bench without the case, and print services accept the included 3MF file as it is.

faq.q: Which USB cable does it need?
faq.a: A USB-C cable that carries data, for the first flash. After that any USB-C charger cable will do.

faq.q: Can I change what it shows?
faq.a: Yes. The firmware is a small PlatformIO project, and the pin numbers are generated from the wiring so they cannot drift apart.
